questions: Tell me a bit about yourself
answer: Isaac Daniel Sudakar is a software developer and technical product manager in Calgary. He has spent 7+ years turning messy manual work into software people actually use, from a Chrome extension running in 11 stores to a resume tool used by 4,000+ job seekers.

questions: What do you do at Calgary Co-op?
Tell me about your current job
answer: Isaac is an IT Operations Specialist at Calgary Co-op. He supports stores and departments across Windows, POS hardware, Active Directory, Entra ID, Intune and Microsoft 365, and builds internal tools when a manual process keeps costing people time.

questions: How many years of experience do you have?
Have you worked in software long?
answer: Isaac has about 7+ years across software, product and operations: IT operations at Calgary Co-op, a web development internship at The Blessed Life, electrical and IoT work at Cris Planners, and teaching and records work at CSC. He has shipped tools in every role.

questions: How did you get into software?
Tell me about your career switch
answer: Isaac started in electrical and electronics engineering, then moved through IoT installations, IT operations and web development. That path taught him to read both the technical system and the human workflow before choosing a solution.

questions: Do you have a product management qualification?
answer: Isaac completed SAIT's Product Management program in 2025 and Project Management program in 2024. He also holds a B.E. in Electrical and Electronics Engineering from Panimalar Engineering College, 2018.

questions: Are you certified in product management?
answer: Isaac holds product marketing, project management and leadership certifications through Credly, including go-to-market strategy, Agile project management, risk and stakeholder fundamentals, plus Microsoft 365 Fundamentals (MS-900).

questions: Do you know React and TypeScript?
What languages and frameworks does he use?
answer: Isaac works with TypeScript, JavaScript, React and Next.js on the front end; Node, Python, SQL, Rust and Kotlin when needed; PostgreSQL, Supabase, Docker and CI/CD around the edges. He also works in IT systems, automation and on-device AI.

questions: How do you approach product management?
How do you decide what to build?
Tell me about your PM style
answer: Isaac starts with the workflow and the constraint, writes a short PRD, then ships the smallest slice that proves the outcome. On Tux and Pocket Resume, that meant cutting features that did not earn their place and measuring the ones that did.

Isaac has led projects end to end rather than managing a large engineering team: gathering requirements, aligning stakeholders, making trade-offs and shipping. At Calgary Co-op he also trains users and coordinates rollouts across 11 stores without a dedicated engineering team.

questions: Are you open to new roles?
What are you looking for next?
answer: Isaac is open to conversations about software developer and technical product manager roles where the work combines engineering, product judgement and real operational problems. Calgary, remote or hybrid all work for him.

questions: What do you bring to a team?
answer: Isaac moves between the code, the product decision and the person doing the work. He has shipped a 4,000+ user product, cut a 4–6 hour store task to under 10 minutes, and built on-device AI without a backend. He finishes things.
Isaac is based in Calgary, Alberta. He has worked with distributed teams and is comfortable remote or hybrid. For the right role he is open to discussing relocation.

questions: Where can I find you online?
How do I get in touch?
answer: Email is the fastest route to Isaac: benisaac1892@gmail.com. He is also on LinkedIn at /in/isaacdani and GitHub at Isaac-1555, and is happy to talk about roles, products or a problem worth automating.

questions: What did you build at Calgary Co-op?
How did you cut the barcode task by 95%?
What is the Chrome extension used in stores?
How much time did the Co-op tool save?
answer: Barcode Lists is a Manifest V3 Chrome extension that replaced a manual FMC barcode and file lookup taking 4–6 hours per session. It now runs in under 10 minutes across 11 Calgary Co-op stores: a 95% reduction, still maintained without a dedicated engineering team.

questions: What is your AI resume project?
Have you built anything with AI?
Tell me about the resume Chrome extension
answer: Pocket Resume is a free Chrome extension used by 4,000+ job seekers. It reads a job posting and rebuilds the user's own resume around it with a deterministic, on-device engine: no API key, no upload, no account, and a tailored PDF in about a second.

questions: Did you build a desktop app?
What is the Rust Tauri project?
answer: Tux is a terminal-first desktop workspace built with Rust and Tauri 2: split PTY terminals, file explorer, live git state, inline diffs and a CodeMirror editor. v1.0.0 ships for macOS, Windows and Linux, with 11 themes and fully rebindable shortcuts.

questions: How does the AI study assistant work?
What did you build with Gemini?
answer: SatBrain turns PDFs, documents and lecture audio into summaries, quizzes, flashcards and charts. It processed 500+ documents in beta and cut study prep time by roughly 70%. Isaac was product manager and lead developer, using Gemini, Supabase and a React SPA.

questions: What is the Android notes app?
How does on-device note routing work?
answer: NoteBucket is a local-first Android app that files notes by meaning. BGE-small runs through llama.cpp on the phone, produces 384-dimension embeddings, and routes notes by cosine similarity. No cloud, no account, zero network permissions, and a 41 MB arm64 APK.

questions: What is your Android media app?
Can you explain the YouTube app?
Have you built a WebView app?
answer: MyTube puts YouTube, YouTube Music, Movies and Anime into one Android shell with isolated WebView profiles, hosts-based ad blocking, background playback, PiP and a real MediaSession. It is a 12 MB signed APK with 11 tagged releases and zero dropped frames in its 1,151-frame PiP test.

questions: What other projects have you built?
Do you contribute to open source?
answer: Beyond the case studies, Isaac has built Ez-Resume, D4C, Summarease, AniRust, CoachGG, BetterYT and Phone Barcode Scanner. Most are open source on GitHub under Isaac-1555, and several started as tools he needed himself.

questions: What kind of teammate are you?
How do you handle messy problems?
answer: Isaac digs into how people actually work before proposing software. He likes small, shippable slices, written decisions and direct feedback, and is comfortable translating between engineering detail and the human side of the problem.

K.I.D is a retrieval assistant, not a generative model. Isaac wrote every answer in advance. The question is embedded in the browser with a small model, matched by meaning to those answers, and returned locally. No API call leaves the page.

questions: Do you send my questions anywhere?
What happens to what I type?
answer: Questions stay in the browser. There is no backend, no API key and no analytics on what is typed. The only network request is downloading the small model once; after that, matching happens on the device.
